subtitle: How Gujarati Cotton Wove the Indian Ocean Together

panels.shot: split wide shot, half showing a Gujarati port warehouse, half a dusty rubbish mound at Fustat with a tiny patterned cloth fragment between them
panels.action: Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay stands in a dim warehouse, hand on a roll of fine printed cotton, while on the other side of the frame a weathered hand in a dusty Egyptian rubbish heap gently lifts a tattered fragment of the same pattern.

dialogue.text: Between a weaver’s loom in Cambay and a rubbish heap in Fustat, a thin cotton cloth carried the weight of a world economy.

i18n.hi: कांबे के करघे से फ़ुस्तात के कूड़े तक, हल्की सूती पर चढ़ा था दुनिया की अर्थव्यवस्था का बोझ

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over Fustat’s rubbish mounds with Cairo in the hazy distance
panels.action: An expansive view of layered rubbish mounds outside medieval Fustat, with scraps of faded textiles half-buried in dust, while beyond them the clustered flat roofs and minarets of Cairo shimmer in the heat.

dialogue.text: In the old city of Fustat near Cairo, broken pots and torn rags lay forgotten in rubbish heaps for centuries, quietly preserving the traces of far coasts.

i18n.hi: काहिरा के पास पुराने फ़ुस्तात में, टूटे घड़े और फटे चिथड़े सदियों तक कूड़े में पड़े रहे, चुपचाप दूर तटों के निशान बचाते हुए

panels.shot: close-up macro shot of a textile fragment being lifted by gloved modern hands, focusing on the pattern
panels.action: Modern conservator’s gloved fingers gently lift a small, tattered cotton fragment from the earth, its fine red and black block-printed pattern still visible against the frayed white threads.

dialogue.text: When these scraps were unearthed and carried to museums in Cairo, Oxford and New York, scholars saw more than rags; they saw Indian cotton, dyed and printed for a distant market.

i18n.hi: जब ये चिथड़े निकाले गए और काहिरा, ऑक्सफ़र्ड, न्यूयॉर्क के संग्रहालयों में पहुँचे, विद्वानों ने कपड़ा नहीं, भारतीय सूती देखी, दूर बाज़ार के लिए रंगी‑छपी हुई

panels.shot: medium shot of a museum display case with several labelled Fustat fragments
panels.action: A museum display case shows several mounted textile fragments from Fustat, each with intricate repeating designs, under soft lights, while dim silhouettes of visitors look on beyond the glass.

dialogue.text: Collections in the Ashmolean, the Victoria and Albert, the Metropolitan and others gathered hundreds of such fragments, many from Fustat, each a clue to the routes of cloth.

i18n.hi: एशमोलियन, विक्टोरिया ऐंड अल्बर्ट, मेट्रोपॉलिटन व दूसरे संग्रहों ने ऐसे सैकड़ों टुकड़े जुटाए, कई फ़ुस्तात से, हर एक कपड़े की राह का सुराग

panels.shot: close-up on the structure of a Fustat fragment, threads and dye visible
panels.action: An extreme close-up reveals the fine, even cotton yarns in a fragment, with areas of deep red, soft brown and black forming crisp motifs, and faint outlines where resist dyeing left the cloth pale.

dialogue.text: Technical studies of the threads and dyes showed a signature look: fine cotton, mordant-dyed reds, resist reserves, and block-printed lines linked to workshops in western India, especially Gujarat.

i18n.hi: धागों और रंगों की जाँच में एक पहचान उभरी: महीन सूती, मर्दन्ट से जमे लाल, रिज़िस्ट की खाली जगहें, और ब्लॉक‑प्रिंट की रेखाएँ, सब पश्चिमी भारत, ख़ासकर गुजरात के कारख़ानों से जुड़ी

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of a weaving shed in Cambay, shafts of light illuminating looms
panels.action: Inside a modest weaving shed in Cambay, Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay leans over a wooden loom, bare feet on the pedals, as sunlight slants across ordered warp threads and hanging skeins of cotton.

dialogue.text: Centuries earlier, in towns like Cambay on the Gujarat coast, anonymous weavers sat at low looms, turning local cotton into plain cloth that would become the canvas for dyes and stamps.

i18n.hi: सदियों पहले, गुजरात तट के कांबे जैसे कस्बों में, गुमनाम जुलाहे नीची करघियों पर बैठते, देसी सूती से सादा कपड़ा बुनते, जो आगे रंग व छाप का कैनवास बनता

panels.shot: medium shot of the weaver passing cloth to dyers and printers in an alley workshop
panels.action: Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay rolls up a finished bolt of pale cloth and passes it through a narrow lane to neighbouring dyers, where men stand beside vats and carved wooden blocks stacked on shelves.

dialogue.text: The weaver’s work was only the first step; dyers and printers took over, their yards crowded with vats, drying lines and wooden blocks carved with repeating patterns.

i18n.hi: जुलाहे की मेहनत बस पहला पड़ाव थी; रंगरेज़ और छापछापे आगे बढ़ते, उनके अहाते कड़ाहों, सूखती डोरियों और एक‑सरी नक़्शों वाली नक्काशीदार लकड़ी की छापों से भरे

panels.shot: close-up of hands applying mordant and placing a carved block onto cloth
panels.action: The hands of Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay, now working as a printer, carefully brush a mordant mixture onto a carved wooden block and press it firmly onto the cotton, leaving a precise pattern of tiny dots and vines.

dialogue.text: Mordants rich in metallic salts were painted or stamped onto the cloth; when the fabric later met the red dye, only those touched areas fixed the colour, while the rest stayed pale.

i18n.hi: धातु‑भरी मर्दन्ट स्याहियाँ कपड़े पर बनाई या छापी जातीं; जब कपड़ा लाल रंग से मिला, तो बस वही छुई जगहें रंग थामतीं, बाकी फीकी ही रहती

panels.shot: wide shot of a dyers’ yard with resist-dyed cloths drying on lines
panels.action: In an open yard, Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay and fellow artisans hang long cotton lengths on ropes; some have portions coated with waxy resist, others already show red and black motifs, as vats of dye steam nearby.

dialogue.text: Resist pastes guarded areas from the bath, keeping them light; alum and iron mordants drew in reds and blacks, building layered designs that matched tastes in the Islamic lands to the west.

i18n.hi: रिज़िस्ट लेप ने रंग से हिस्सों को बचाया, उन्हें हल्का रखा; फिटकिरी और लोहे के मर्दन्ट ने लाल‑काले खींच लिए, परत‑दर‑परत नक़्श बने, जो पश्चिम के इस्लामी देसों की पसंद से मेल खाते

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on patterns that echo Islamic geometric and vegetal motifs
panels.action: Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay holds up a finished cloth showing repeating stylised palmettes in neat rows, interlaced with small geometric borders reminiscent of mosque tilework, examining the alignment of the motifs.

dialogue.text: Some patterns echoed the geometry and stylised foliage of Islamic art, not by accident; designs were adapted so that Indian cloth would fit comfortably into Egyptian and West Asian households.

i18n.hi: कुछ डिज़ाइन इस्लामी फ़न की ज्यामिति और बेल‑बूटों की गूँज थे, यूँ ही नहीं; नक़्श बदले गए ताकि भारतीय कपड़ा मिस्र और पश्चिम एशिया के घरों में सहज घुल जाए

panels.shot: wide shot of Cambay harbour bustling with activity and bales of cloth being loaded
panels.action: On the crowded waterfront of Cambay, Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay watches as porters carry bundled bolts of cloth on their shoulders toward waiting dhows, while merchants in robes tally goods beside the water.

dialogue.text: From Cambay’s tidal creeks, bales of cotton left the artisans’ lanes and entered the world of merchant capital, where guilds and trading houses controlled ships, credit and contacts across the Indian Ocean.

i18n.hi: कांबे की खाड़ी से, रुई के गट्ठे कारीगर गलियों से निकलकर सौदागर पूँजी की दुनिया में उतरे, जहाँ हाथियों और साहूकारों के घरों से जहाज़, उधार और हिन्द महासागर भर के रिश्ते चलाए जाते

panels.shot: medium shot contrasting the weaver receiving payment with a richly dressed merchant counting profits
panels.action: Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay receives a small weighed-out payment from a middleman in a simple shop, while in the background a richly dressed merchant sits on cushions counting stacked coins and reading a letter.

dialogue.text: The weavers and dyers knew the chemistry and craft, but much of the profit flowed upward to merchants, who advanced cash, fixed prices and commanded the cargoes that sailed west.

i18n.hi: जुलाहे‑रंगरेज़ रसायन और हुनर जानते थे, पर मुनाफ़ा ऊपर के सौदागरों को बहता, जो नकद देते, दाम बाँधते और पश्चिम जाती खेपों का हुक्म चलाते

panels.shot: long shot of a sewn Arab dhow on the Arabian Sea under a starry sky
panels.action: A stitched-plank dhow leans into the wind on the moonlit Arabian Sea, its lateen sail full, bolts of cloth stowed under a woven deck, as sailors watch the stars and a faint shoreline fades behind.

dialogue.text: Sewn-plank dhows carried these cottons up the Arabian Sea, past the Gulf of Aden and into the Red Sea, their pilots reading currents and stars long before maps fixed the routes in ink.

i18n.hi: जुड़ी‑तख़्ती वाले धाऊ ये सूतियाँ लेकर अरब सागर चढ़तीं, अदन की खाड़ी पार कर लाल सागर में घुसतीं, उनके मल्ल नक़्शों के बनने से बहुत पहले धाराएँ और सितारे पढ़ते

panels.shot: wide shot of Fustat’s riverfront with warehouses and markets along the Nile
panels.action: On the banks of the Nile at Fustat, warehouses open onto the river as boats unload bales, while narrow streets lead into dense markets crowded with traders, donkeys and shaded stalls.

dialogue.text: Fustat, a hub of the Fatimid and later Egyptian worlds, received these loads; from its warehouses cottons spread into Cairo’s lanes, rural villages and beyond, leaving threads in many lives.

i18n.hi: फ़ातिमी और फिर मिस्री दुनिया के बड़े ठिकाने फ़ुस्तात ने ये खेपें उतारीं; गोदामों से कपड़े काहिरा की गलियों, देहात के गाँवों और आगे तक फैल गए, कितनी ज़िंदगियों में धागे छोड़ते हुए

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a modest Fustat home reusing Indian cloth as household linen
panels.action: Inside a modest Fustat dwelling, a worn but still patterned Indian cotton serves as a curtain over a doorway, while another fragment lines a storage chest, with children and a woman moving around their daily tasks.

dialogue.text: Not every cloth became a luxury robe; many fragments in Fustat come from reused fabrics, turned into curtains, linings and wrappings in ordinary homes before being discarded and buried in trash.

i18n.hi: हर कपड़ा शाही पोशाक नहीं बना; फ़ुस्तात के कई टुकड़े पुराने कपड़ों के हैं, जो आम घरों में परदे, अस्तर और लपेटन बनकर चले, फिर कचरे में फेंके और दब गए

panels.shot: close-up of a Cairo Geniza letter being unrolled on a desk
panels.action: A Jewish merchant unrolls a long, narrow letter on a wooden desk in a dim room, Aramaic and Judaeo-Arabic script flowing across the page, as an oil lamp casts light on inked words about goods and prices.

dialogue.text: In another corner of this world, the Cairo Geniza preserved letters of merchants, studied later by Goitein, speaking of Indian cloth, prices, risks and partners along the same routes traced by the textiles.

i18n.hi: इसी दुनिया के दूसरे कोने में, काहिरा की गनीज़ा में सौदागर पत्र सँभले रहे, जिन्हें बाद में गोइतिन ने पढ़ा, जहाँ भारतीय कपड़ों, दामों, ख़तरों और इन्हीं राहों के साथी भागीदारों का ज़िक्र था

panels.shot: split close-up between a Geniza merchant letter and a Fustat textile fragment
panels.action: One half of the frame shows the inked lines of a Geniza letter mentioning Indian textiles; the other half shows a surviving Fustat cotton fragment, their edges aligned as if two halves of a single record.

dialogue.text: Together, the written contracts of the Geniza and the dyed fragments from Fustat make one of the clearest proofs that medieval Indian textiles were not legend, but daily fact in the Mediterranean.

i18n.hi: मिलकर, गनीज़ा के लिखित सौदे और फ़ुस्तात के रंगे टुकड़े ये साफ़ सबूत बने कि मद्ध्यकालीन भारतीय वस्त्र किवदंती नहीं, बल्कि भूमध्य सागर की रोज़मर्रा हक़ीक़त थे

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition showing the same pattern at loom, in Fustat home, then under museum glass
panels.action: A triptych-like scene shows Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay lifting a fresh printed cloth from his loom, a middle panel shows that cloth decades later hanging in a Fustat home, and the final panel shows its fragment under glass in a modern museum.

dialogue.text: Ruth Barnes and other scholars traced these journeys, not to name single workshops, but to show how an artisan’s pattern could travel from a lane in Cambay to a household in Fustat and finally to a display case.

i18n.hi: रुथ बार्न्स और दूसरे विद्वानों ने इन सफ़रों के धागे पकड़े, किसी एक करख़ाना की तलाश नहीं, बल्कि ये दिखाने को कि एक कारीगर का नक़्श कांबे की गली से फ़ुस्तात के घर और आख़िर में शो‑केस तक पहुँच सकता है

panels.shot: slow push-in on the weaver’s thoughtful face as he touches the cloth, with faint superimposed map lines of the Indian Ocean
panels.action: Gujarati Textile Weaver of Cambay sits quietly, fingertips resting on a folded cloth, as faint, ghostly outlines of the Indian Ocean and the Red Sea hover around him, hinting at distant lands he will never see.

dialogue.text: A single piece of cotton, born from Gujarat’s looms and baths, stitched itself into the economy of three continents, reminding us that even the smallest fragment can carry the shape of a world.

i18n.hi: एक अकेला सूती टुकड़ा, गुजरात के करघों और रंगघरों से निकला, तीन महाद्वीपों की अर्थव्यवस्था में सिल गया, याद दिलाता कि सबसे छोटा चिथड़ा भी पूरी दुनिया की शक्ल ढो सकता है

subtitle_i18n.en: How Gujarati Cotton Wove the Indian Ocean Together
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे गुजराती सूती ने हिन्द महासागर को जोड़ा
